words.gram: 2 sg. impv. √vid (Vedic lengthened form of viddhi)
m. voc. sg., bahuvrīhi (puru-vasu, Vedic lengthening purū-)

hindi: हे मघवन्, जानो, मार्ग को जानो; दिशाओं को बता दो। हे शक्तियों के स्वामी, हे अनेक पुरातन शक्तियों के स्वामी, हे बहुधन, हमें सहायता दो।
english: Know, O Maghavan, know the way; point out the directions. Help us, O lord of powers, of the many ancient powers, O rich in wealth.
notes: The '~' in gātumanuśa~siṣo transliterates the candrabindu (anunāsika) standing for anusvāra: anuśaṃsiṣaḥ. vidā and śikṣā are Vedic imperatives with lengthened final vowel; vidā could also be read as 2 sg. subjunctive. pūrvīṇām may be 'of many' (puru) or 'of the former, ancient' (pūrva); both senses are given. The object of śikṣā ('us') is not in the text.

words.gram: n. nom. sg. (sung with pluta svā3r)

words.gloss: O attentive one, O wise one

words.gram: acc. pl. encl. (visarga lost before i)

hindi: इन सहायताओं से तुम, सूर्य के प्रकाश के समान, किरण के समान हो; हे प्रचेतन इन्द्र, हमें यश और अन्न-बल के लिए प्रबुद्ध करो।
english: With these aids you are like the light of heaven, like a ray; O attentive one, O Indra, make us aware, for splendour and for strength.
notes: svā'3rnnā~śuḥ is doubtful: the apostrophe and 3 are the pluta mark (ऽ३), not an avagraha, and the '~' is the candrabindu. The reading taken is svar + na + aṃśuḥ ('like heaven's light, like a ray'; n doubled after r, na + aṃśuḥ -> nāṃśuḥ), on the model of 645 'aṃśur na śociḥ'. No finite verb is in line 1 ('you are' is supplied). Parallel: the Aitareya-Āraṇyaka text of this Mahānāmnī has a refrain 'evā hy evā hy evā hi' between the two lines, which this edition does not print here (not applied). na in 'na iṣe' is naḥ, not the particle 'like'.

words.gram: m. voc. sg. (n doubled before vowel)

hindi: ऐसा ही है: शक्र धन के लिए और बल के लिए है, हे वज्रधारी। हे सबसे बलवान वज्रधारी, तुम आगे बढ़ते हो; हे सबसे उदार वज्रधारी, तुम आगे बढ़ते हो। यहाँ आओ, पीओ, आनन्दित हो।
english: Thus indeed is Śakra for wealth and for strength, O wielder of the thunderbolt. O most mighty wielder of the thunderbolt, you hasten forth; O most bountiful wielder of the thunderbolt, you hasten forth. Come hither, drink, be exhilarated.
notes: Line 1 has no finite verb; 'is' is supplied. ṛñjase is taken as 2 sg. present middle of √ṛj/ṛñj 'to hasten, strive towards'; some take it as a dative infinitive ('to reach'). The '~' in ma~hiṣṭha is the candrabindu for anusvāra (maṃhiṣṭha). In vajrinnṛñjasa the final -a is -e of ṛñjase before the following ā (Vedic sandhi).

hindi: धन के लिए वीरों से भरा बल पाओ; इच्छाओं के अनुसार बलों के स्वामी बनो। हे सबसे उदार वज्रधारी, तुम आगे बढ़ते हो, तुम जो वीरों में सबसे बलवान हो।
english: Find heroic strength for wealth; be lord of strengths according to our wishes. O most bountiful wielder of the thunderbolt, you hasten forth, you who are the mightiest of heroes.
notes: bhavo = bhavaḥ (2 sg. subjunctive/injunctive of √bhū with imperative sense) before v-. vaśā~ anu = vaśān anu (acc. pl. with anunāsika before a vowel), 'according to the wishes'; whose wishes is not stated ('our' is supplied in English). suvīryam may also be 'wealth in heroes'.

words.gloss: O wise one, O observant one

hindi: जो उदारों में सबसे उदार है, किरण के समान, ज्वाला के समान — हे ज्ञानी, हमें आगे ले चलो। इन्द्र ऐसा ही जाना जाता है; उसी की स्तुति करो।
english: He who is the most bountiful of the bountiful, like a ray, like a flame: O wise one, lead us onward. Indra is known as such; praise him indeed.

text_flags.why: possible: the typed Devanagari has a candrabindu after a halanta म् and no vowel a before śu; the expected sandhi maghonām + aṃśuḥ gives maghonām aṃśur (the a of aṃśuḥ seems lost in typing).

notes: Read as maghonām aṃśur na śociḥ, matching 642 and 648. vide is taken as 3 sg. perfect middle 'is known' (it can also be 'knows'); the sentence division 'indro vide | tam u stuhi' is one reading, another is 'Indra knows; praise him'. The relative yaḥ has no main clause of its own; the comparison 'like a ray, like a flame' is read with it.

words.gram: 3 sg. aor. subj. (root uncertain, see notes)

hindi: शक्र ही स्वामी है; उसे हम सहायता के लिए पुकारते हैं, उस विजेता को जो कभी पराजित नहीं हुआ। वह हमें शत्रुताओं के पार ले जाए; वही संकल्प है, छन्द है, महान् ऋत है।
english: Śakra indeed is master; him we call for help, the conqueror who is unconquered. May he carry us beyond hostilities; he is will, the hymn, the lofty cosmic order (ṛta).
notes: svarṣat: the form and root are uncertain; it is taken, with the traditional sense, as 'may he carry (us) across / bring us safely over' (an s-aorist subjunctive), governing ati dviṣaḥ. Others connect it with svar 'light' ('may he win light beyond the foes'). kratuś chanda ṛtaṃ bṛhat is a verbless list of nominatives; 'he is' is supplied. chandaḥ may be 'metre' or 'delight'.

hindi: धन की प्राप्ति के लिए हम इन्द्र को पुकारते हैं, उस विजेता को जो कभी पराजित नहीं हुआ। वह हमें शत्रुताओं के पार ले जाए; वह हमें शत्रुताओं के पार ले जाए।
english: We call Indra for the winning of wealth, the conqueror who is unconquered. May he carry us beyond hostilities; may he carry us beyond hostilities.
notes: The second line repeats the half-verse 'sa naḥ svarṣad ati dviṣaḥ' twice, as printed (a refrain). On svarṣat see 646.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (initial a elided, avagraha)

words.gloss: O good one, O giver of wealth (Vasu)
you take up, you set down

hindi: हे पत्थर के धारी, पहले के सवन का जो तुम्हारा सोम-रस है, वह आनन्द के लिए है। हे वसु, हमें अपनी कृपा में रखो; हे सबसे बलवान, तुम्हारी पूर्ति की प्रशंसा की जाती है। शक्र ही अब सचमुच वशी है; उस नये स्तोत्र को तुम स्वीकार करते हो।
english: That Soma-stalk of yours from the earlier pressing, O wielder of the stone, is for exhilaration. Place us in your favour, O good one; your bounty, O most mighty, is praised. Śakra indeed is now the master; that new praise you take up.
notes: pūrvasya 'of the earlier' has no noun; 'pressing' (of Soma) is supplied in translation, the text says only 'of the earlier'. adrivo~'śur = adrivo 'ṃśur: anunāsika plus avagraha for the elided a of aṃśuḥ. sumna = sumne (loc.) before ā. 'navyam' has no noun; 'praise' is supplied (the new thing is not named). saṃnyase is uncertain: taken as 2 sg. middle of sam-ni-√as 'you lay down / take in'; it could also be a dative infinitive ('for laying down'). pūrtiḥ 'fulfilment' is taken as Indra's gift; 'your' is supplied.

words.gram: m. voc. sg. (epenthetic t before s)

hindi: हे जनों के प्रभु, हे वृत्र के हन्ता, संग्रामों में हम दोनों परस्पर बात करें — तुम वह वीर हो जो गौओं के बीच जाता है, अति स्नेही मित्र, छल से रहित।
english: O lord of the people, O slayer of Vṛtra, let us two speak together in the contests, you the hero who goes among the cows, a most kindly friend, free from duplicity.
notes: bravāvahai is 1st dual subjunctive middle ('let us two speak'); who the two are (singer and Indra) is not stated. 'goṣu gacchati' is literal 'goes among the cows' (i.e. to win cattle); not interpreted further. The nominatives śūraḥ, sakhā, suśevaḥ, advayuḥ describe the one addressed.

hindi: ऐसा ही है। ऐसा ही है, हे अग्नि। ऐसा ही है, हे इन्द्र। ऐसा ही है, हे पूषन्। ऐसा ही है, हे देवगण। ओम्। ऐसा ही है, हे देवगण।
english: Thus indeed. Thus indeed, O Agni. Thus indeed, O Indra. Thus indeed, O Pūṣan. Thus indeed, O gods. Oṃ. Thus indeed, O gods.
notes: Closing formula of the Mahānāmnī. The first token is 'evā hi' sung with a prolonged stobha 'o3 o3 o3 vā' (the apostrophes before each 3 are the pluta mark ऽ३, not avagrahas); the stobha is not translated. The '|' tokens are the edition's daṇḍas inside the line, kept as tokens. 'oṃ' before the final 'evāhi devāḥ' is printed as the sign ॐ. The short phrases have no verb; 'is' is supplied in translation. GROUPING: none; the edition's grouping of the two lines is kept.
